title: Ending a subject and acknowledging farewell

captions.physics: Changing replies when an occasion disappears
captions.emotions: Feeling farewell to a familiar subject

meaning: When the occasion for a familiar discussion disappears, you can give the conversation a clear conclusion and acknowledge sadness about a subject that connected your exchanges.
text: The Wheel of Fortune in the physical position of your Vishuddha appears in conversation changing when its earlier occasion disappears. The World in energy supports the wish to complete the exchange, naming what is settled and which question no longer needs an answer. Death in emotions brings farewell to a familiar subject. You can end the discussion sensibly and gently while still feeling the loss of a known place it held in communication.

For example, you have been discussing possible participation in an amateur storytelling evening, but the event is cancelled. Instead of another choice of remarks, you conclude that the invitation no longer needs its original answer. **A clear ending leaves room for sadness**. You can say that you enjoyed inventing an account together for that evening. Cancellation ended a particular subject without making your interest wasted. Sadness concerns both the event that will not happen and the familiar conversation about it now left behind.

Wanting to finish becomes rigid if it requires never mentioning the subject without a practical reason. A clear conclusion then turns into a ban on experiencing loss. The World’s constructive wholeness helps include the conversations’ significance in the ending. You can recognise a closed question while retaining room to say why it mattered; farewell does not require finding a new shared subject immediately.
